documents.body:
Interval check. Up once a night at most now. Pain flares about every 3-4 weeks, short, at home with fluids and rest. Folate and hydroxyurea daily, no missed doses he can think of. Avoiding ibuprofen.

Vitals ok. Mild pallor, flow murmur, lungs clear, abdomen soft.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PHYSICAL

27 y/o, here for his yearly. Doing well. Nocturia stays at 0-1. Pain flares at his usual pace, none severe. Energy good. Mentions he and his wife are starting to talk about having kids next year.

Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: Well. Mild pallor, sclerae clear. Thyroid normal. RRR, soft systolic flow murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, spleen not felt. No edema, no leg ulcers. Neuro nonfocal.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Sickle cell on hydroxyurea: CBC/retic/LDH today.
- CKD 2 / hyposthenuria: CMP and urine albumin/creatinine (yearly per nephrology).
- Folate deficiency: on daily folic acid.
- Flu and COVID vaccines given.
- Follow-up visit in November, labs every 3-4 months.

documents.title: Records for wife's OB
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my wife's OB wants me to come to a preconception visit with her in March to talk about the sickle cell side of things for a baby. They asked for my records. Can you send them? I signed their release form.

documents.title: RE: Records for wife's OB
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Andre, we received the release and faxed your problem list, medication list, recent labs and the nephrology letter to the OB office this morning.

documents.title: Preconception Counseling - Partner
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY PRACTICE
Preconception counseling, 03/09/2026. Copy to the partner's primary care physician.

Andre Mensah, 28, attended today with his wife, who is our patient, to plan for a pregnancy. Outside records from his primary care office reviewed: sickle cell trait per his records, history of vaso-occlusive pain episodes, hyposthenuria, folate deficiency, CKD stage 2. Medications: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily. No known drug allergies. Family history: father with sickle trait, a maternal cousin with sickle cell disease, mother with hypertension. Never smoker, no alcohol; works as a software developer.

The couple's main question was whether a child of theirs could end up carrying the sickle gene without being ill from it, and how likely that is.

Counseling: we went over how the sickle hemoglobin change is passed on, one gene copy from each parent, and how the effect on a child depends on whether one or two altered copies are inherited. His wife's carrier status is the key unknown: her hemoglobin electrophoresis has not been done yet. We explained what each possible result would mean for their children in general terms and that we would go through the specific chances once her result is back. Genetic counseling referral offered for after her testing.

Plan: hemoglobin electrophoresis for his wife, ordered under her chart. Revisit as a couple when resulted. No changes to his care from our side.

Outside OB/GYN practice

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First visit since the fall (November visit was cancelled; spring lab draw did not happen). Feels well. Pain flares unchanged, every few weeks, short, at home. Night voiding once at most with the fluid routine. Taking hydroxyurea and folic acid daily. Went with his wife to her OB's preconception visit in March; letter on file.

Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily. NKDA.

O: Vitals normal. Well appearing. Mild pallor, anicteric. RRR, flow murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no spleen tip. No CVA tenderness. No edema or leg ulcers.

A/P:
1. Sickle cell (trait per records, disease course) on hydroxyurea: CBC with retic today, overdue. Continue.
2. Folate deficiency: on folic acid daily.
3. Hyposthenuria / CKD 2: CMP today; urine albumin at the fall physical.
4. Refills sent for both meds.
Physical in the fall.

documents.body: Hi Andre, Friday's labs look like your usual: blood count and reticulocytes where they always sit, kidney function steady. Nothing to change. Next blood count in the fall.
